ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: In the image, AC is the diagonal line connecting point A and point C; A, B, C form triangle ABC, where AB and BC are adjacent sides of the rhombus. The problem gives AB=10, ∠ABC=120°. Because ABCD is a rhombus, all sides are equal, so BC=AB=10. Use the law of cosines in triangle ABC: AC^2=AB^2+BC^2-2·AB·BC·cos120°=10^2+10^2-2·10·10·(-1/2)=100+100+100=300. Therefore AC=√300=10√3.

method.method_draft: Place the rhombus in coordinates. From the image, orient AB as the lower side and AC as the vector from A to the opposite vertex C. From the text, AB=10 and angle ABC=120°. Since adjacent angles in a parallelogram/rhombus are supplementary, angle DAB=60°. Set A=(0,0), B=(10,0). The side AD has length 10 and makes a 60° angle with AB, so AD=(10cos60°,10sin60°)=(5,5√3). Then C=B+AD=(15,5√3). Hence AC=√(15^2+(5√3)^2)=√(225+75)=√300=10√3.
